text:
For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity and a **2,600 W inverter**, giving you more buffer for the igniter at startup and for campsite extras. The cited estimate is roughly **450–750 Wh for a 12-hour cook**, so this station should have capacity for about two or three cooks, depending on your grill and what else you plug in. [Source](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

If you only need **one cook**, a station around **1,000 Wh** may be enough. Pellet smokers typically draw just **35–60 W after ignition**, but the igniter briefly draws much more; check your smoker’s startup requirements and the station’s surge rating before buying. [Sizing guide](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)

Keep the station dry and well away from the grill’s heat, grease, and ash. If you’ll also run lights or charge devices, choose the larger capacity.
